summary: ```markdown # How To Use Color Switch | Clo Feature Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey all you Clovers, it's Phoebe, and I have a really cool update for you regarding colors, texture switching, and more. So let's jump in and have some fun while we learn! ## Overview of Corsets Here I have three corsets, and we're going to do two things to two of them. The first one here is going to stick with being the original. The second one, we're going to switch it out with a color. And this third one, we're also going to switch out with a color. ## Property Editor and Recolor Options In my property editor down below, you can see my base color map along with a new recolor option. It says "recolor," followed by "desaturate" and "switch." - **Desaturate**: We all know how to use it, and it changes the entire art by reducing the saturation. - **Switch**: This is the new feature we’re focusing on today. Many of you may already be familiar with it from the multi-texture editor videos. ## Using Desaturate For the first corset, we're going to use the desaturate option. 1. Select **Desaturate**. 2. Go to **Color** and switch it out with a screen. 3. Hit **Apply** and **Close**. With desaturate, as you all know, we can increase the intensity and play around with the brightness. However, this method changes the whole art and doesn’t preserve the true texture, print, or repeat. ## Utilizing the Switch Feature Now, for the third corset, we're going to use the same green color, but instead of desaturating, we'll use the switch feature. 1. Hit **Switch**. 2. Observe how it takes one of the colors in the print and switches it out with the green. At the top, we can add in the green just to see what happens. ### Color Change Options You have three options for changing out colors: - Add the color on top. - Desaturate the color. - Switch out a color. ## Multi-Texture Editor A few other facts about the color switch: it works exactly the same as our color switch in the multi-texture editor. For those of you who might be wondering, "Phoebe, what's a multi-texture editor?" It's a fantastic feature we've had for quite some time now in Cloud. 1. Go to your base color map. 2. Open the texture editor by clicking on the dots. 3. In the texture editor, you can select your fabric. The color switch is checked on by default, which allows for automatic color selection. ### Customizing Multi-Colored Prints If you have a multi-colored print and want to switch out two, three, or even four colors, you can do that. 1. Increase the color count (e.g., three colors). 2. Select colors to switch out with green or other desired shades. 3. Hit **Apply** and **Close**. Now, you can see how easy it is to switch out multiple colors and keep the texture close to the original artwork. ## Conclusion The switch feature is incredibly useful for keeping colors and textures closer to the original while allowing for color changes. I'm really excited about this update, and I believe it will make all of your color changes much cooler and more fun! Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, feel free to use the comment section below. For more learning, check out our channel, and don't forget to like and subscribe for updates on our new videos. Keep on having fun in Cloud! ```
